Then, we translated this average speed into its corresponding speed bin; for example, an average speed of 20 mph for a given segment of driving would belong to speed bin 5. For each vehicle on each hour, day type, and road type, we sum the total amount of time from the segments that occurred in each average speed bin. Additionally, for each vehicle on each hour, day type, and road type, we summed the time from the segments spent in all the average speed bins. These two calculations are used to determine the amount of time spent in each speed bin relative to all speed bins, referred to as the speed distribution. 27 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. We used Equation 1 to calculate the speed distribution for each individual vehicle, road type, day ID, and hour ID.
